structureTypeSource: Great Lakes 2T-1A-2: welded 4130 steel-tube fuselage, fabric covered; wooden-spar wings (Great Lakes 2T-1A-2 maintenance manual).
_wingStructureNote: Contact damage (Ty 2026-11-03). Break station = the N-strut on both wings, |y| 2.875 (tools/own_models/build_great_lakes.py YI). The own model has four ailerons and slave struts, but this flight config carries aileron rows on the LOWER wing only, so there is no slaved aileron to model here: see AGENT-LOG NEEDS YOU.

spinAero.shadowKSource: Geometric helical shadow depth (TailWake.GeometricShadow): the share of dynamic pressure a fully shadowed strip loses. Replaces the Report 648 wake correlation for EVERY surface of this type, and brings in the fuselage's own shadow on the tail and the wings (TailWake.BodyStation). Ty 2026-11-08: "expand the shadow work to all 6 shipping aircraft include the shadow effects of the fuselage on the tail and wing's too". 0.5 is the depth fitted on the Pitts against the owner's spin attitudes on 2026-11-08, and it is a PHYSICAL statement - half the q is gone where a wake fully covers a section - rather than a per-type fudge, so the six carry the same number until a type's own evidence moves it. What differs between types is the geometry, which is the point: the Pitts' cellule shadows itself, the Extra's stabiliser spans well outside its fuselage and is barely shadowed at all (measured in a tumble: tail q 1.00 -> 0.96), and the fuselage's own shadow is what takes the fin in an upright flat spin while leaving it in clear air inverted.
spinAero.stabHighAlphaKSource: Extra lift-curve slope on the HORIZONTAL tail over 60-90 deg of its own local flow: what lets the stabiliser hold the nose where a flat spin puts it, and the key the Pitts' upright flat spin was fitted on. THE PITTS' OWN SHIPPED VALUE, carried here unrefitted. Ty 2026-11-10, flying the plate tails: "The Great Lakes has similar overly flat and overly difficult upright flat spin recovery. Inverted is fine" - and 2026-11-09, on the attitude itself: "Tweak the stab for 80 nose down not 85". 1.9 is what that instruction was fitted to on the Pitts, and it lands this type on the same target. MEASURED UPRIGHT, BeggsTimingProbe (BEGGS_T=1 BEGGS_TYPE=great-lakes-like), Ty's own Pitts entry flown unchanged on this type - developed flat-spin alpha, then turns to stop rotating on Beggs-Mueller. finK\stabK: 0.0/1.0 (as this type shipped) -> alpha 85.4 and NEVER recovers; 0.0/1.4 -> 82.4, 8.36 turns; 0.0/1.9 -> 79.3, 4.49 turns (11.1 s), out at alpha 18.2; 0.5/1.0 -> 83.6, never; 0.5/1.4 -> 80.1, 5.07; 0.5/1.9 -> 76.1, 3.07. BOTH HALVES OF HIS REPORT MOVE on the stab alone: 85.4 -> 79.3 deg, and never -> 4.49 turns. (Re-read on the tip that carries the fleet re-rig of 2026-11-10, which solved a different propeller for the five fitted-blade types; it moves every cell here by 0.1-0.4 deg and no conclusion. FINSIDEWASHK WAS MEASURED AND DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN, and this is the part to read before anyone adds it. On the UPRIGHT side 0.5 is clearly better (3.01 turns against 4.42, which is nearer the real aeroplane's turn or two), and on GEOMETRY it belongs here: the term is amp = 1 + k*(R/r)^2 on a vertical strip's lateral flow, k is a property of the model (potential flow past a cylinder peaks at the top and bottom of a body in side-on flow, where a fin stands), so what decides whether a type carries it is how much fin area stands within a body-depth of the body mid-line - and the area-weighted mean amplification at k 0.5 is Pitts 1.420, GREAT LAKES 1.411, Extra 1.319. This type's fin sits in the Pitts' crossflow to within 0.6 %.) IT WAS NOT TAKEN BECAUSE IT BREAKS THE INVERTED SPIN, which Ty's own report says is already right (InvSpinPowerHoldProbe, INVHOLD=1 INVHOLD_ID=great-lakes-like; INVHOLD_FINK / INVHOLD_STABK were added for this). Mean alpha of the held power-on inverted spin, finK\stabK: 0.0 -> -66 (as shipped) / -64 / -62 at stabK 1.0 / 1.4 / 1.9, reading -61 after the re-rig; 0.5 -> -59 at 1.4, -55 at 1.9. The whole stabK sweep costs 4 deg; the fin costs 7 more, and at 0.5/1.9 it takes the spin to mean alpha -54.9, which fails InvertedSpinPowerTests.FullPowerAndProSpinAileronHoldTheInvertedFlatSpin's < -55 - the Christen Eagle reality check that Ty reported broken twice. So 1.9 ALONE is what ships: it is the whole of his stated attitude target and most of the recovery, for 4 deg of inverted attitude instead of 11, and it leaves the pinned inverted check green. THE OPEN QUESTION FOR TY, which is a flying judgement and not a number: adding finSidewashK 0.5 buys 4.42 -> 3.01 turns of upright recovery and costs 7 more degrees of inverted flat-spin attitude. If he flies 1.9 and still calls the upright recovery "overly difficult", 0.5 is the next step and the inverted pin is the thing to re-judge with him, not to relax quietly. DO NOT GO PAST 0.5 IF IT IS EVER ADDED: 0.9 is the Pitts' inverted-spin cliff (pitts-s2b-like.json finSidewashKSource - 0.8 holds alpha -85.7, 0.9 collapses it to -68.2), and 0.5 is the value Ty put back after flying 0.9. NOTHING IN ORDINARY FLIGHT MOVES: the term is gated on 60-90 deg of the stabiliser's own local flow, which a trimmed cruise, a climb and an ordinary stall do not reach - this type's Vso, trim alpha and trim elevator are unchanged, and so is the hands-off trimmed cruise.
spinAero.controlSpoilerKSource: A deflected control on a BROADSIDE surface acts as a spoiler on the separated wake, not as a flap: adds k*sin(delta)*|sin(alpha_chord)|*q*S normal to the FIXED surface's own plane, over hinged tail strips only, ramped in over 20 deg from controlSpoilerOnsetDeg. 0.6 is the PITTS' value and is carried unchanged, not refitted per type: it was fitted there on 2026-11-10 to Ty flying a clip of his own Pitts flat spin ("the elevator literally does nothing in the spin"), and pitts-s2b-like.json holds the sweep it came from - elevator authority at alpha 80 of 3.7 deg/s2 at k 0, 15.5 at 0.3, 27.4 at 0.6, 43.4 at 1.0, where 1.0 leaves the curve nearly flat from 30 to 90 deg and a plate should not be. WHY THIS TYPE HAS IT NOW. It shipped on the Pitts and the Extra alone, and that was STAGING rather than a finding: the argument for the term is about the SECTION - post-stall the section law is Cd_max*sin(theta), which is flat at broadside, so a strip model gives a control on a broadside surface a direction to point its force in and no magnitude to command - and when this type's horizontal tail became a flat plate on 2026-11-10 (b7396cd0: stall 9 deg, Cl_max 0.90, blend 44) that argument started applying to it too. Worse, the controlSpoilerOnsetDeg 10 that came with the plate was INERT here, because the spoiler block in AeroModel.Compute is gated on controlSpoilerK > 0.0: the onset was moving the start of a term multiplied by zero, and the hole it was meant to close was being closed by the 44 deg blend alone. Ty 2026-11-10, shown exactly that and the argument that the restriction to two types was staging: "Do it". MEASURED ON THIS TYPE (SpoilerFleetProbe, SPOILER_FLEET=1). Authority is the pitching moment the stick's whole travel commands at 30 m/s with the wind turned to the body alpha asked for, as a fraction of its own alpha 0 value; the floor is the worst of it over alpha 10-60 at a 0.5 deg step. Floor 0.109 at alpha 40 -> 0.214 at alpha 40; alpha 45 0.192 -> 0.308. IT COSTS THE PITCH DAMPING NOTHING, and for a mechanical reason rather than a lucky one: the term carries sin(gain*deflEff) and is gated on a non-zero deflection, so it cannot appear in a controls-neutral quantity, and dM/dq is one. VERIFIED rather than asserted, because if it had moved then the gate would not be what we think it is: the worst dM/dq over alpha 10-60 is BIT-IDENTICAL at k 0 and k 0.6 on all eleven configs that gained it and on the two that already had it. Vso AND THE TRIM ARE UNMOVED TOO, which was not obvious and had to be measured rather than argued: unlike stabHighAlphaK's 60-90 deg band, this term opens at 10 deg of the strip's OWN flow, and a tail strip with the stick near its aft stop at the stall is not self-evidently below that. It is - measured on the Stearman at its own Vso, the stabiliser's local angle is 2.74 deg against the 10 deg onset, because the downwash (3.49 deg there) and the stabiliser's own negative incidence take it out of the body alpha - so the ramp never opens in any ordinary flight condition and every type's Vso, trim alpha and trim elevator come out unchanged to the digit. WHAT IT DOES CHANGE is high-alpha pitch authority and therefore the spin, which is the point, and nothing below the ramp.
spinAero.controlSpoilerOnsetDegSource: The spoiler ramp starts at the SECTION'S OWN STALL. 30 deg was chosen when every hStab was a naca0012 (stall 14 deg); a flat plate stalls at 9-12, which left alpha 20-34 with no table effectiveness and no spoiler yet - and that band WAS the hole in the elevator authority. Worth the whole difference: authority floor 0.165 at onset 30 against 0.249 at onset 10. Ty 2026-11-10 accepted the plate knowing this moves the term he judged the Pitts' spin on.

construction._comment: Crash-in-water damage (Core/Wreck, lane/claude-crash-water 2026-11-02). Welded steel-tube fuselage and wooden wings, doped fabric covering. Two tandem OPEN cockpits, measured from the own model (tools/own_models/build_great_lakes.py CKP, v6 off the N3765F three-view; docs/models/great-lakes-own-PROVENANCE.md): elliptical openings, front x -0.97..-1.33 half-width 0.19 m, rear x -1.64..-2.08 half-width 0.215 m; area pi*a*b.

propulsion.dryBoundaryExcessSource: Dry boundary friction excess at rest, over the power curve's own running friction intercept (PistonEngine.BoundaryFrictionFactor): 2.19 means this engine resists 3.19x its running friction when it is dead and dry. Lycoming AEIO-360, 361 cu in, 4 cyl, CR 8.7. SOLVED 2026-11-10 (lane/claude-boundary-friction, CompressionStopProbe with COMPSTOP=1 SOLVE=1) against Ty's anchor "Cranking resistance should be calibrated such that at fine pitch the prop stops right at level flight stall speed", and then his "fix it per engine": it is the one value that puts the measured stopping speed on this type's OWN stall speed, 22.9 m/s = 51 mph (PracticeScenario.EstimateVso, sea level, flaps up - the number the rest of the suite is tuned against, not a book figure). Solved and not predicted: nothing inside an engine explains the fleet's spread, because motoring friction and rated torque both scale with displacement - see PistonEngine.BoundaryExcessFor for what was tried and rejected. THIS IS NOW THE ONLY THING IN THE DEAD-ENGINE MODEL THAT IS FITTED TO ANYTHING: the compression peak beside it is the engine's own gas load out of its displacement and compression ratio (PistonCompression.PeakNmFor), and the speed a stopped propeller breaks away at is a measurement rather than an anchor. Re-solving moves it about 0.1 because the sweep that measures the stopping speed steps 0.25 m/s. The fleet default for every type not yet solved is 3.0.
propulsion.pitchStopSource: PUBLISHED, not derived: FAA TCDS A18EA Rev 11 gives the Hartzell HC-C2YK-4F/FC7666A-2 as low 12.5 deg and high 26.8 deg at the 30 in station. Ty's two rules derive 14.20/23.86 — again narrower at both ends; see the note on pitts-s2b-like. The same sheet also settles the diameter: EXACTLY 74.0 in, 'no reduction allowed', which is what propDiameterM already holds (1.8796 m). The 76 in figure belongs to the 140 hp FIXED-PITCH variant of this type.
propulsion.propInertiaSource: Propeller + spinner + the crank's rotating parts, kg.m2. From the OWNER'S BLADE RULE (2026-11-09, tools/aircraft_builder/prop_inertia.py): each blade is 15 % of the net propeller weight with its centre of mass at 25 % of the DIAMETER from the axis, the rest being hub near the axis - because a heavy constant-speed hub contributes almost nothing to sum(m r^2), so a mass-weighted estimate overstates the couple. M 24.5 kg, D 1.88 m, 2 blades: blades 1.623 + hub 0.172 (k 0.10 m) + crank 0.09 = 1.88, against 5.0 before. MASS: ASSUMED ~50 lb with spinner, Hartzell HC-C2YK-4F 74 in (docs/aircraft/great-lakes-inertia-DERIVATION.md). AEIO-360, four cylinders. VALIDATION: the rule reproduces Hartzell's published two-blade polar moment to +18 % (1.412 against 1.198) and runs +60 % high on their three-blade one, so it is applied to two-blade types only.
propulsion.coarseOnOilLossSource: Ty 2026-11-10: "aerobatic aircraft with a constant speed propeller default to high pitch with loss of oil pressure like twins do (Seminole beech 18 etc) and standard single engines default to low pitch with no oil pressure". Oil holds these blades FINE, so losing it drives them COARSE - a twin's path to feather, and on an aerobatic single what stops the prop overspeeding pointed down.

gear.toeOutDegSource: Standard 2 degrees of toe-out on every taildragger's mains (Ty 2026-11-10: "Use 2 degrees toe out on all taildraggers standard unless I adjust based on feel"). A standing slip angle outboard on each wheel: level the pair cancel, and when one is loaded more its outboard side force is the larger, pushing the aeroplane back toward the light side - "The loaded tire tries to unload back to the other". The sign comes from each wheel's own y, so one value means outboard on both (LandingGear.ToeRad). Live-tunable in OPTIONS while flying.
gear.gearTypeSource: Air-over-oil shock strut (build_great_lakes.py, from the 2T-1A-2 layout: "oleo shock strut"; the model has Gear_OleoTop_L/R). The spring is an oleo and the LINKAGE still swings, which is why the two are authored apart: a telescopic strut would have no legPivot.
gear.legPivotSource: Measured off great-lakes-like-own.glb, which has the linkage rigged: Gear_Pivot_L at span 0.050, up -0.830 -- the half-axle's U-joint on the fuselage centreline (build_great_lakes.py: "axle U-joint hinge at the fuselage centreline (Gear_Pivot_L/R), compression strut aft to the lower longeron fitting") -- and the wheel touching at span 1.079, up -1.482. 1.03 m out, 0.652 m down: splay 0.63, half a Cub's, because a half-axle from the centreline is a long arm.

gear.gearTypeSource: Air-over-oil shock strut (build_great_lakes.py, from the 2T-1A-2 layout: "oleo shock strut"; the model has Gear_OleoTop_L/R). The spring is an oleo and the LINKAGE still swings, which is why the two are authored apart: a telescopic strut would have no legPivot.
gear.legPivotSource: Measured off great-lakes-like-own.glb, which has the linkage rigged: Gear_Pivot_L at span 0.050, up -0.830 -- the half-axle's U-joint on the fuselage centreline (build_great_lakes.py: "axle U-joint hinge at the fuselage centreline (Gear_Pivot_L/R), compression strut aft to the lower longeron fitting") -- and the wheel touching at span 1.079, up -1.482. 1.03 m out, 0.652 m down: splay 0.63, half a Cub's, because a half-axle from the centreline is a long arm.
gear.toeOutDegSource: The matching value for THIS wheel. Toe is per leg (LandingGear.ToeRad reads g.ToeOutDeg and takes the sign from the wheel's own y), so a value on one main and nothing on the other is not 2 degrees out on both -- it is 2 out on one wheel and dead straight on the other, a standing uncancelled side force of about 0.42 of that wheel's load (12 per rad x 2 deg) with nothing opposing it. The 2026-11-10 toe-out commit says "Sixteen types, both mains each" and wrote the field to the FIRST main only on fourteen of them; this is the other main on each, with the same number. Ty's knob (LandingGear.ToeOutOverrideDeg) always covered both, which is why the two types he was flying when he chose the number -- the Pitts and the Extra, the two the commit did write both -- felt right.

cellule._source: Derived biplane lift interference (BiplaneCellule: a Biot-Savart lattice on this config's own wings; Prandtl NACA Rep. 116, Munk NACA Rep. 151 General Biplane Theory 1923). ON because naca2312 peaks at CLmax 1.450, a true 2-D value, so the interference is not already in the table. Not a tuned number: nothing here is fitted to a stall speed.

loading._cgLimitsSource: FAA TCDS A18EA Rev. 11, Model 2T-1A-2 (docs/WEIGHT-AND-BALANCE.md): datum = centre of the most forward lateral fuselage tube, located at body x -0.200 (MAC 46.0 in with its leading edge at Sta. 9.0, and the firewall route 25 mm away: anchor MEDIUM, +/-25 mm), so body x = -0.200 - arm x 0.0254. C.G. range (+20.0) to (+23.8), one range at all weights: forward -0.708 m, aft -0.80452 m. Gross: maxTakeoffMassKg 816.47 = 1800 lb. These are the stations the 2026-10-30 percent-MAC envelope maps back to on this config's wing.
loading._comment: seats[].eye is the seated pilot's EYE (owner Ty, approved 2026-10-31), body frame +x fwd, +y right, +z DOWN, measured on extended gear; the Cockpit camera sits exactly there. The PRIMARY seat is first. loading.seats[].station, loading.tanks[] and loading.baggage[] are the arms from docs/pending/loading-arm-estimates.md (Codex lane, 2026-11-01): a published TCDS/POH arm where the row is CONFIRMED, converted to this frame through that aircraft's anchor. maxKg is the published placard where the source gives one. referenceKg is UNCHANGED and still follows the 172's convention, so the reference loading reproduces the authored mass, CG and inertia exactly and nothing moves at spawn. Whether each airframe's authored massKg includes a pilot or fuel is still the open W&B decision in AGENT-LOG NEEDS YOU.
loading._legacyEmptyMassKgNote: the older weight-and-balance lane (e4755c9) authored emptyMassKg as a true EMPTY WEIGHT, excluding pilot and fuel. The current LoadingConfig reads that same key as 'what is left when every station is empty', and these types have no stations in the current schema, so every spawn loaded the aeroplane to its empty weight: the Great Lakes flew 258 kg light (816 -> 558), the Cub 206 kg (553 -> 347), the Swift 50 kg (330 -> 280). SessionSettings.ApplyLoadTo runs on EVERY spawn, so this was the flying mass in the game while the .NET tests, which do not call ApplyLoad, kept using the authored massKg. Set to 0 so it derives from mass.massKg again; the authored figure is kept below, unread, for the open W&B decision in AGENT-LOG NEEDS YOU.
loading._seatPlacardNote: maxKg is a CONVENTIONAL occupant placard (250 lb, and the J-3's own authored 300 lb), not a figure read from a POH. referenceKg follows the 172's convention: the primary seat carries the pilot that mass.massKg already includes, so the reference loading still reproduces the authored mass, CG and inertia exactly and nothing moves at spawn. Whether each airframe's authored massKg really includes a pilot is the open W&B decision in AGENT-LOG NEEDS YOU.
loading._eyeNote: seats[].eye lowered 2026-11-01 after Ty flew build 2026.1101.0733: the rear eye at z -0.487 sat 110 mm ABOVE the top of the rear windscreen glass, so the level sightline cleared the screen entirely and the view was over the frame at the cowling, with the top wing's leading edge across it. Measured against great-lakes-like-own.glb: the rear screen's glass spans glTF y 0.167..0.377 and the front's 0.176..0.350. Each eye now sits where the level sightline passes through the MIDDLE of its own screen - rear glass from -13.5 to +13.8 degrees of elevation, front from -16.5 to +16.3 - and holds out to +-20 degrees of azimuth. The seat STATIONS are weight-and-balance arms and are unchanged.
